subject: 9C2659CEFAA5E6114DDA8A2D71F13AF2
introduction: When a friend mentioned Jesus speaking with Moses and Elijah on the mountain, ‘Abdu’l-Bahá answered that the faithful are always in such company. This guide gathers what the Bahá’í writings say of that company, the Concourse on High: that it consoles the bereaved and the deprived, stands in ranks to aid whoever serves, listens to the songs and prayers of the faithful, watches, rejoices, laments, and welcomes those who die. The scriptures of Israel, the Church and Islam are full of the same host: Jacob’s ladder, Elisha’s chariots of fire, Isaiah’s seraphim, the cloud of witnesses, the angels who descend on the steadfast and say “fear not”. They also set the limits. Jesus would not call the twelve legions; an angel refuses John’s worship; Paul warns against a religion of angels. Shakespeare’s Lorenzo thinks we cannot hear the music while we wear this muddy vesture, and Hobbes and Feuerbach ask whether there is anything to hear but ourselves.
questions: Hebrews speaks of “so great a cloud of witnesses” and Paul of being “a spectacle … to angels”. What does it change in a person’s conduct to believe that he or she is watched and accompanied in this way?
Jesus says he could summon twelve legions of angels and does not. How should the martial language of readings 17 to 23 be understood beside that refusal?
An angel tells John, “See thou do it not … worship God”, and Paul warns against the worship of angels. How do the readings keep the Concourse a fellowship of servants and not an object of devotion?
Lorenzo says we cannot hear the heavenly harmony in this life; the readings say “listen”. What kind of hearing do they mean?
Hobbes and Feuerbach would explain the Concourse as dream or projection. Which of the guide’s claims would survive their reading, and which would not?

outside.why: The friend’s question began from this scene: on a high mountain Jesus is transfigured, and Moses and Elias appear, talking with him.
“The faithful are ever” in such company. Hebrews, after its roll of the dead: we also are compassed about with so great a cloud of witnesses.
The children of martyrs are addressed as their remembrances. Precious in the sight of the Lord is the death of his saints.
The dwellers of the celestial realms rejoice at a soul’s ascension. Jesus speaks of joy in the presence of the angels of God over one sinner that repenteth.
“The angel of the Abha Kingdom is the companion of every deprived one.” In Gethsemane there appeared an angel unto him from heaven, strengthening him.
“Be raised up with the virtues of the Supreme Concourse.” Be ye therefore perfect, even as your Father which is in heaven is perfect.
A prayer to be guarded in the stronghold of protection. The angel of the Lord encampeth round about them that fear him, and delivereth them.
A gathering of two races becomes “the magnet of the Concourse on high”. Where two or three are gathered together in my name, there am I in the midst of them.
Can you paint on the page of the world the pictures of the Celestial Concourse? Thy will be done in earth, as it is in heaven.
“This is a good meeting … it is heavenly.” Jacob waking at Bethel: surely the Lord is in this place; and I knew it not. This is none other but the house of God.
The guardian angels are called “Divine Powers”. Are they not all ministering spirits, sent forth to minister for them who shall be heirs of salvation?
Hobbes observed that to say God spoke to a man in a dream is to say no more than that he dreamed God spoke to him. How would one tell protection by unseen powers from the belief in it?
When they attain these qualities the hosts will assist them. The Qur’an: those who say, Our Lord is God, and afterward are upright, the angels descend upon them, saying: fear not nor grieve.
The hosts “are arrayed in ranks … awaiting”. Elisha’s servant sees the mountain full of horses and chariots of fire round about.
The Supreme Host is engaged in combat. At Badr the believers are promised: I will help you with a thousand of the angels, rank on rank.
The hosts wait to see who will enter the field. Jesus, arrested, says he could have more than twelve legions of angels for the asking, and does not ask. What is the unseen army for, if not rescue?
An army of invisible angels. Milton: thousands at his bidding speed, and post o’er land and ocean without rest.
Whenever we are threatened they rush to our aid. He shall give his angels charge over thee, to keep thee in all thy ways.
The Concourse takes pride in a soul who arises to praise God. Whosoever shall confess me before men, him shall the Son of man also confess before the angels of God.
The holy ones “yearn to return unto this world” to serve. Peter says of the gospel: which things the angels desire to look into.
A house of worship to be raised with grace. I was glad when they said unto me, Let us go into the house of the Lord.
Where noble souls assemble, heaven is near. Jacob dreamed a ladder set up on the earth, and the top of it reached to heaven: and behold the angels of God ascending and descending on it.
Music is praiseworthy at the Threshold. Praise him with the sound of the trumpet: praise him with the psaltery and harp.
A song to stir the dwellers of the Supreme Concourse. When the morning stars sang together, and all the sons of God shouted for joy.
The ears of the Concourse hearken to thy melodies. John heard the voice of harpers harping with their harps, and a new song before the throne.
The dwellers on high laud the faithful on earth who raise their praise. A multitude of the heavenly host praising God: glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace.

Every breath a melody that reaches the Concourse. Lorenzo says the smallest star sings like an angel, but whilst this muddy vesture of decay doth grossly close us in, we cannot hear it. The readings tell their hearers to listen. Who is right about what can be heard?
A melody that “awakeneth the slumberers”. Awake thou that sleepest, and arise from the dead.
“Listen to the Supreme Concourse and hear the call.” Isaiah heard it in the temple: one cried unto another, Holy, holy, holy, is the Lord of hosts.
The Concourse has raised its cry of glory. The voice of many angels round about the throne, ten thousand times ten thousand, saying, Worthy.
As long as love is in the heart, messages from the Concourse continue. The angels and the Spirit descend therein, by the permission of their Lord, with all decrees.

Gabriel is the intermediary of revelation. Feuerbach held that such figures are human powers set outside ourselves: theology is anthropology. What would be lost, and what kept, if the Concourse were read his way?
Such a soul banishes the Evil One from the heart. Resist the devil, and he will flee from you. Draw nigh to God, and he will draw nigh to you.
“These cities are not on earth; they are in heaven.” Our conversation is in heaven.
“The Fire of Moses hath flamed forth!” The bush burned with fire, and the bush was not consumed.
From the realms above comes praise for the steadfast. Well done, thou good and faithful servant.
“All the Concourse on high … are watching.” Paul of the apostles: we are made a spectacle unto the world, and to angels, and to men.
The Concourse is delighted by news of the friends’ firmness. I have no greater joy than to hear that my children walk in truth.
“The angels of heaven pray for thee.” The Qur’an: those who bear the Throne ask forgiveness for those who believe: our Lord, Thou comprehendest all things in mercy.

Angels intercede for thee. Paul warns the Colossians against anyone who would beguile them into a worshipping of angels, intruding into things not seen. What keeps talk of the Concourse on the right side of his warning?
If you seek the kingdom of wealth, attach yourself to the Concourse on high. The kingdom of heaven is like unto treasure hid in a field.
Their faces shall shine in the Most Exalted Kingdom. They that be wise shall shine as the brightness of the firmament.
Having reached that station, be trustworthy with the treasuries of knowledge. Keep that which is committed to thy trust.
Present this merchandise “in the market place of the jewellers of the Concourse”. A merchant man, seeking goodly pearls.
God has forgiven and numbered thee among the devout. The father saw him a great way off, and ran, and fell on his neck, and kissed him.
“O seeker of pilgrimage to the sanctuary of the Supreme Concourse!” My soul longeth, yea, even fainteth for the courts of the Lord.

A station “round which circle the Concourse on High”. When John falls down before the angel who showed him the city, he is told: see thou do it not; I am thy fellowservant; worship God. The Concourse too is pictured as worshipping, not worshipped.
Sea and ocean speak in praise. Praise ye him, sun and moon: praise him, all ye stars of light.
The Concourse rejoices, “yet most of the people are as dead”. The light shineth in darkness; and the darkness comprehended it not.
“The Concourse on High hath attentive ears.” The Qur’an: We know what his soul whispereth to him, and We are nearer to him than his jugular vein.
The Concourse beholds evil doings and shuns the doers. The Lord saw that the wickedness of man was great, and it grieved him at his heart.
When his spirit ascended, the Concourse welcomed him. The beggar died, and was carried by the angels into Abraham’s bosom.
Bunyan of Mr. Valiant-for-truth: so he passed over, and all the trumpets sounded for him on the other side.
A brother now circles the Concourse. Horatio over Hamlet: good night, sweet prince, and flights of angels sing thee to thy rest.
The heavenly body that Christ meant. It is sown a natural body; it is raised a spiritual body.
Blessed is the lowly one who showed humility. He that humbleth himself shall be exalted.
Upon them pray the Concourse on High. The Qur’an says God and His angels shower blessings on the Prophet, and bids believers do likewise.
“Your name is … mentioned in the Concourse on High.” Rejoice, because your names are written in heaven.

shortfall: Many of the readings are single sentences assuring a correspondent that the Concourse on High praises, watches or welcomes; a companion was given to each kind of assurance and not to each letter.

matthew-twelve-legions-of-angels.text: Thinkest thou that I cannot now pray to my Father, and he shall presently give me more than twelve legions of angels

corinthians-spectacle-unto-angels.text: for we are made a spectacle unto the world, and to angels, and to men

luke-confess-before-the-angels.text: Whosoever shall confess me before men, him shall the Son of man also confess before the angels of God
